name: Ironbridge Gorge Wild Garlic
short_description: Spectacular spring garlic in the gorge woodland.
description: The steep wooded slopes of the Ironbridge Gorge are carpeted with wild garlic each spring, with the best picking along the riverside footpaths between Ironbridge and Coalbrookdale.

name: The Wrekin Bilberries
description: The open heathland of The Wrekin produces a reliable crop of bilberries (whortleberries) each summer, particularly on the upper south-facing slopes above Little Hill.

name: Coalbrookdale Community Orchard
short_description: Heritage fruit in the cradle of industry.
description: A community orchard in the heart of Coalbrookdale featuring traditional Shropshire apple and pear varieties, maintained by local volunteers and open for public picking.

name: Telford Town Park Blackberries
short_description: Brambles along the park's wild margins.
description: The wilder hedgerow and scrub margins of Telford Town Park are lined with productive blackberry bushes, particularly along the paths towards Hollinswood and the ski slope.

name: Wellington Community Orchard
description: A volunteer-managed community orchard on the edge of Wellington featuring local heritage apple, plum, and damson trees, open to the public throughout the autumn season.

name: Incredible Edible Telford Town Centre Planters
short_description: Urban food growing in the shopping heart.
description: Community growing planters around the town centre precinct and Southwater area featuring herbs, salad leaves, and seasonal vegetables for all to help themselves.

name: Granville Country Park Sloes
short_description: Blackthorn hedges on former pit land.
description: The reclaimed colliery land of Granville Country Park is criss-crossed with blackthorn hedges, providing excellent sloe picking each October alongside hawthorn haws.

name: Buildwas Abbey Meadow Wild Greens
description: The damp water meadows and stream margins around Buildwas Abbey support patches of wood sorrel and watermint, with riverside watercress accessible along the Severn bank.

name: Madeley Wood Hazelnuts
short_description: Ancient hazel coppice above the gorge.
description: Hazel trees in the semi-ancient woodland above Madeley and along the gorge escarpment produce reliable crops of nuts, best gathered before the squirrels beat you to them.

name: Lightmoor Village Community Planters
short_description: New community growing in an eco-village.
description: Raised planters throughout the Lightmoor eco-village grow seasonal vegetables and edible herbs, tended by residents and open to the wider community.

name: Dawley Bank Wild Damson
short_description: Hedgerow damsons on old pit spoil lanes.
description: Wild damson and bullace trees grow in the hedgerows and rough ground along the old lanes of Dawley Bank — a classic Shropshire hedgerow fruit.

name: Lilleshall Sweet Chestnuts
short_description: Mature chestnut trees by the monument.
description: Mature sweet chestnut trees stand in the woodland near Lilleshall Monument and the old abbey grounds, yielding a good crop of nuts each October.

name: Stirchley Grange Elder
short_description: Elder along the community farm hedgerows.
description: Elderflower and elderberries are plentiful in the hedgerows and rough margins around Stirchley Grange farm and local nature area.

name: Lawley Common Rosehips
short_description: Rose hedges on the common edge.
description: Dog rose bushes lining the field boundaries and common edges of Lawley produce a heavy crop of rosehips each autumn, perfect for syrup making.

name: Apley Woods Wild Garlic and Blackberries
description: The mature broadleaf woodland at Apley Woods offers wild garlic carpets in spring and productive brambles along the open path edges in late summer.
